max rel. error, analytic mu_s vs the pip.name: max rel. error, analytic mu_s vs the pipeline's free convolution
max rel. error, analytic mu_s vs the pip.why: same premise as Stages 1 and 2a; a relative density error lies in [0,1] and 1e-4 is two orders above the comparison's 1e-6 floor

|bias at the largest n_seed minus Stage.name: |bias at the largest n_seed minus Stage 1's analytic reading|
|bias at the largest n_seed minus Stage.why: a finite reference must approach the analytic one as n_seed grows; a relative-bias difference is non-negative and 10 is a stated practical ceiling. 1.5x the resolution allows for the largest seed still being finite

|bias| at n_seed = 4096, the science's o.name: |bias| at n_seed = 4096, the science's own seed size
|bias| at n_seed = 4096, the science's o.why: a relative bias against a known answer; the bar is the gate's own resolution at this ensemble, so MISSED means the finite reference costs nothing this instrument can see

fitted exponent of |bias| against n_seed.name: fitted exponent of |bias| against n_seed
fitted exponent of |bias| against n_seed.why: d log|bias| / d log n_seed. A sampling cost must DECAY, so the bar is negative; +3 and -3 bracket anything a finite-sample term can plausibly do, and a positive exponent (growing with n) would indicate a bug rather than a sampling cost

bandwidth spread of |bias| at n_seed = 4.name: bandwidth spread of |bias| at n_seed = 4096
bandwidth spread of |bias| at n_seed = 4.why: max minus min |bias| across the bandwidth nodes; non-negative, 10 a stated practical ceiling. Stage 1 measured this as zero to every printed digit with a perfect reference, so any resolvable value here is introduced BY the finite reference

instrument.model: Gate D against a FINITE empirical reference

params.name: n_seed
params.why: THE axis. The science's reference is F_empirical of exactly n=4096 seed points; this brackets that by 8x either way so the cost can be seen to SCALE rather than just to exist at one size

params.name: eps_over_delta
params.why: Stage 1 found the reading identical at every bandwidth with a PERFECT reference. Whether a finite reference introduces bandwidth dependence is this cell's whole reconciliation with the audit, so the bandwidth must be swept, not fixed

params.name: eta
params.why: sets the true statistic. Stage 1 learned this the hard way: an additive floor over a shrinking truth explodes while a bias does not, and a finite reference is a candidate source of exactly such a floor

params.name: seed_realisations
params.why: the reference is now RANDOM, so a single draw would confound the reference's systematic cost with one realisation's luck. Averaged over draws; the spread is reported

params.name: k_flow
params.why: the largest k on the science's dense grid, matching Stage 1

params.name: replicates
params.why: configurations per (seed, eta); with 8 seed draws this is 64 readings per cell, the ensemble Gate D's resolution is quoted at

params.name: configuration
params.why: the TRUTH is held exact while only the reference changes. That isolation is the cell's design: a deviation here cannot be the configuration's fault because the configuration is unchanged from Stage 1

scope: RECERT_SCOPE Stage 2b. Holds the TRUTH exact and changes only the REFERENCE to the science's own finite-empirical style. Refits nothing; the configuration is Gaussian-perturbed rather than flowed.
